title: Copy-and-modify with line position (after Timm 2014)
statement: Words are produced as a mixture of copying a word seen in the last 20 words of the page with at most one glyph changed, a line-position vocabulary (first, interior, last word), a memorized vocabulary, and a glyph-trigram speller; weights fitted on the training pages. On practice the copy component earns a small share (weight 0.044) and lowers held-out cost from 11.312 to 11.286 bits per word against the same model without copying (bag of words 11.586, letters only 11.400): copying recent words helps predict the text, but most of the gain comes from position and spelling.
